entry = await rlm.harness.create_memory(title='Continual-ARC: decode colored marks on tiled grid intersections', path='continual_arc', global_=True, content='''Solved task-c5508678. Reusable rule: A large grid has a repeated tile texture (the output background color) and a regular lattice of separator/intersection points. Identify the lattice spacing and sample the separator value at its intersection points. Ignore points holding the ordinary separator color; special colors are marks. Crop the lattice to the bounding rows/columns containing any special marks, then consider each adjacent 2×2 block of lattice points. The corresponding output cell is the repeated tile/background color unless all four corner samples are the same special color, in which case output that color. Thus each output cell represents a uniform colored 2×2 corner square; isolated/partial marks do not transfer. Output dimensions are (number of active lattice rows−1) × (number of active lattice columns−1); do not include unmarked outer lattice rows/columns. Verified on demos: task-c5508678 output background is the tile interior (2 in demo1, 9 in demo2, 0 in demo3); special corner squares copy their mark color. For its test, active lattice was rows r3..r18 and columns c2..c26, producing 5×4 output. One initial attempt was wrong because it included unmarked outer lattice rows; trim to active marked bounds.''')
print(entry.id)
